source.title: Landscape Connectivity and Dropout Stability of SGD Solutions for Over-parameterized Neural Networks

record.file_problem: none; full paper and supplementary material are present
record.tranche_reason: The paper studies dropout stability and loss-landscape connectivity, not the training-error outcomes, mechanisms, or interventions named by V1–V6. It reports test-set classification results after training, which do not establish training classification error.
record.gate_note: The paper's discussion of spurious minima and its citations to prior optimization work are not its own results. Its own CIFAR-10 results use test-set features and report population risk and classification error; the text does not report training classification error.
record.test_reason: The study proves dropout stability and connectivity between SGD solutions and measures test-set performance after neuron removal. These results do not measure training classification error, convergence to spurious minima in teacher-student problems, or the interventions in V3–V6. Connectivity does not establish that SGD avoids suboptimal minima.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: under their assumptions, the authors prove width-dependent dropout stability and approximate connectivity between SGD solutions, and experiments show decreasing degradation after neuron removal. These guarantees do not establish convergence to global minima or absence of spurious minima.
record.recipe_differences: The paper uses one-pass or online SGD with square loss in its theory and mini-batch SGD minimizing cross-entropy in its experiments; its results concern dropout stability and connectivity, rather than the claim versions' training-error tests.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported dropout degradation varies with network width, architecture, and dataset.

fits_no_version.finding: At width 3200, removing and rescaling half the neurons leaves test error near the full network's level on MNIST and CIFAR-10 features.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Wide trained fully connected networks can retain test performance after removal and rescaling of half their neurons.

fits_no_version.finding: Test-error degradation after removing half the neurons decreases with width across the reported architectures and datasets.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing width improves post-training dropout stability.

fits_no_version.finding: Under stated assumptions, population-loss barriers along constructed paths between SGD solutions vanish with increasing width and sufficiently small step sizes; experiments illustrate approximate connectivity.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Overparameterized SGD solutions can be connected by paths with small loss barriers.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML), Proceedings of the 37th International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 119, 2020
record.problems: The experiment's classification errors are evaluated on the test dataset, so they do not answer the training-error claim. The text gives several width-dependent degradation values but does not state their uncertainty. The experiments use VGG-16 features for CIFAR-10; the paper notes that fully connected networks trained directly on CIFAR-10 images have larger classification error but does not quantify it in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No additional separately stated numerical result rows were omitted. Other plotted trajectories and width sweeps are figure-only and are not transcribed as numerical values.

untested.parts: Training classification error of convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/100, including random labels and model-size, stopping and regularization comparisons.
Spurious-minimum frequency in realizable two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems and the effect of one or two extra student neurons.
Training-error degradation with depth, identity shortcuts, and special initialization or normalization-free recipes.
Effects of activation-matched initialization and orthogonality on training speed, signal propagation and trainable depth.
Initial stability thresholds, transient loss recovery, curvature evolution, edge-of-stability behavior and divergence.
Batch normalization's effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and comparison with Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: Section 5 does report training-loss plateaus of 0.062 on MNIST and 0.415 on CIFAR-10 at width 3200. Thus, not every reported loss is test-set loss; these cross-entropy values still do not establish V1's training classification error or convolutional-network claim. Different initialization distributions in the connectivity experiments do not constitute a training-speed or trainable-depth comparison for V4.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error, random or corrupted labels, CIFAR-100, and the stated model-size, stopping, and regularization comparisons.
Teacher-student ReLU problems, spurious-minimum frequency, and student width relative to teacher width.
Plain versus residual shortcuts, depth-related training error, normalization, and the cited special training recipes.
Initialization comparisons, signal or gradient propagation, and trainable depth.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, loss recovery, sharpness, and divergence.
Batch-normalization comparisons, training speed, learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup.
